title: Private English tutor in Ho Chi Minh City: rates and the law
description: Why freelance tutoring is unpermitted work for foreigners in Vietnam, the legal ways to earn extra, 2026 HCMC and online rates, and how side income is taxed.
h1: Private tutoring and online teaching in Vietnam: what is legal, what it pays, how it is taxed
intro: You can earn extra by tutoring English in Ho Chi Minh City, but not legally as a freelancer. Paid work needs a work permit tied to an employer, and the simple sole-trader registration is open only to Vietnamese citizens, so cash private lessons risk a fine and deportation. The lawful route is extra hours through a licensed centre, school or company that holds a permit for you. Teaching online for a platform abroad is a legal grey area, and if you are tax-resident that income is taxable in Vietnam.
keyPoints: There is **no lawful freelance-tutor route** for a foreigner: a work permit belongs to one employer, household businesses are for Vietnamese citizens only, and working without a permit costs {{vnd:15000000-25000000}} plus possible deportation (Decree 283/2026/ND-CP, from 10 September 2026).

Circular 19/2026 took general English enrichment out of the "extra teaching" rules of Circular 29/2024. That removed a registration rule, not the work-permit requirement. Never tutor pupils you teach at school for money.

The legal ways to earn more are extra hours with your own employer, or a second employer that gets its own work permit for you. Centres in Jul–Oct 2026 ads paid {{vnd:390000-600000}} an hour, most new-teacher offers {{vnd:430000-560000}}.
Online platforms pay far less than Saigon centres: Cambly pays US$10.20 an hour, and Preply keeps the first trial lesson with each student plus 18–33% after that.

Teaching online for a Vietnamese company needs a work permit; for a company abroad it is a grey area. If you are tax-resident (183 days or more in Vietnam, or leases adding up to 183 days), you must declare platform income yourself, because nobody in Vietnam withholds it.

sections.title: Is private tutoring legal for foreigners in Vietnam?

blocks.text: Not as freelance work. No regulation names foreign private tutors, but the rules that do exist leave no lawful route. Paid work in Vietnam needs a work permit, and under [Decree 219/2025/ND-CP](https://luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/nghi-dinh-219-2025-nd-cp-quy-dinh-ve-nguoi-lao-dong-nuoc-ngoai-tai-viet-nam-407607-d1.html), in force since 7 August 2025, a permit belongs to **one employer**. Working for a second employer, even in the same job, needs a new permit for that employer (Art. 20(1)). Decree 219 has no permit for working for yourself: every form of work it lists is tied to a Vietnamese employer, partner or presence.

Nor can you set yourself up as a sole trader. The household business (hộ kinh doanh), the simplest business form, is reserved for Vietnamese citizens under [Decree 168/2025/ND-CP, Art. 82(2)](https://hethongphapluat.com/nghi-dinh-168-2025-nd-cp-ve-dang-ky-doanh-nghiep/dieu-82). A foreigner who wants to run a tutoring business [needs a company and the investment procedures](https://luatvietnam.vn/doanh-nghiep/nguoi-nuoc-ngoai-co-duoc-thanh-lap-ho-kinh-doanh-561-31579-article.html), which is a different project from a few evening students.

blocks.caption: The rules that decide whether tutoring is legal for a foreigner in Vietnam, as of October 2026 (official texts and legal databases linked in the sources)
rows: Circular 29/2024/TT-BGDĐT on extra teaching (in force 14 February 2025)

Paid tutoring providers outside school must register a business and publish subjects, schedule, venue, teacher list and fees. A teacher may not give paid extra classes outside school to pupils they are assigned to teach. No extra classes for primary pupils except arts, sports and life skills.
Paid extra classes for pupils you teach at school are banned, whatever your nationality.
Circular 19/2026/TT-BGDĐT (in force 15 May 2026)
Foreign-language, STEM, digital-skills, arts and life-skills activities outside the Ministry's subject programmes no longer count as "extra teaching".
General English is mostly outside Circular 29 now, but an English class that re-teaches the school programme may still count. The work-permit rule is untouched.
Decree 219/2025/ND-CP, Art. 20(1)
A permit covers one employer; a second employer needs its own permit.
Your permit does not cover private students, a second centre or weekend classes elsewhere.
Decree 168/2025/ND-CP, Art. 82(2)
Household businesses are for Vietnamese citizens only.
You cannot register as a freelance tutor.
Decree 283/2026/ND-CP (from 10 September 2026)
A worker without a valid work permit (none, or an expired one) is fined; deportation can be added. An employer that uses a foreigner outside the permit's terms is fined separately.
Cash lessons, or work for an employer your permit does not name, expose you to a fine of {{vnd:15000000-25000000}} and deportation.

blocks.text: The circulars are on [LuatVietnam: Circular 29](https://luatvietnam.vn/tin-van-ban-moi/da-co-thong-tu-29-2024-tt-bgddt-quy-dinh-ve-day-them-hoc-them-tu-14-02-2025-186-100582-article.html) and [Circular 19](https://luatvietnam.vn/tin-van-ban-moi/da-co-thong-tu-19-2026-tt-bgddt-sua-thong-tu-29-2024-tt-bgddt-ve-day-them-hoc-them-186-108257-article.html). [VnExpress's explainer](https://vnexpress.net/bo-giao-duc-sua-thong-tu-29-ve-day-them-hoc-them-nhu-the-nao-5060026.html) covers the 2026 changes. The worker's fine and the deportation penalty are reported by [Sức khỏe & Đời sống](https://suckhoedoisong.vn/tu-10-9-2026-lao-dong-nuoc-ngoai-se-bi-phat-neu-khong-co-giay-phep-lao-dong-169260824224738.htm). This is an explanation of the rules, not legal advice; for your own case, ask a Vietnamese lawyer.

blocks.title: A common mistake: lessons on the side of a valid permit
blocks.text: A permit does not cover any teaching you like. It covers one employer, one position and the places that employer notified. Private students, a friend's centre at weekends or a paid trial class elsewhere are all **outside the permit**, which leaves you exposed to the no-permit fine and deportation, and the employer that uses you there is fined as well.

sections.title: Legal ways to earn extra from teaching

blocks.text: Every legal option runs through an employer that holds a permit for you. The [work permit guide](/teach-in-vietnam/vietnam-work-permit-for-english-teachers) explains how that permit is issued; here is what it allows in practice.

items: **More hours with your own employer.** Ask whether your centre runs one-to-one or small-group classes, corporate courses or holiday camps. These should sit inside your existing permit when they are the same job for the same employer; ask the employer to confirm that in writing. Changing your position or form of work with the same employer needs a new permit (Decree 219, Art. 20(2)).

**A second employer with its own permit.** A second centre or school can apply for a separate permit for you. The [Labour Code](https://dulieuphapluat.vn/van-ban/lao-dong/bo-luat-lao-dong-2019-45716.html) gives part-time staff on a labour contract the same rights as full-time staff (Art. 32), and you are paid for the hours on that contract.

**Cover lessons.** Schools short of a teacher pay for cover, but covering for another school is work for a second employer, so the same permit rule applies. See [cover lessons and substitute teaching in Ho Chi Minh City](/teach-in-vietnam/cover-lessons-and-substitute-teaching-in-ho-chi-minh-city).

**Corporate and exam classes through a company.** Business English and IELTS work usually reaches foreign teachers through a centre or a teacher-supply agency, which is your employer for permit purposes. See [teaching IELTS in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/teaching-ielts-in-vietnam).

**Your own company.** Running a tutoring business means setting up a company and going through the investment procedures, not a quick registration. For other ways to grow beyond classroom hours, see [career paths for English teachers](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teacher-career-path-in-vietnam).

blocks.text: Calling the arrangement "freelance" does not change it. Under [Labour Code Art. 13(1)](https://hethongphapluat.com/bo-luat-lao-dong-2019/khoan-1-dieu-13), any agreement with paid work, a wage and one side's management or supervision is a labour contract, whatever it is called. A "service contract" with a single centre that sets your timetable is a labour contract in substance, but it cannot support a work permit on its own, so you end up working without one.

sections.title: Teaching online from Vietnam: the legal position

blocks.text: It depends on who pays you. **Teaching online for a Vietnamese company or platform needs a work permit**, exactly like classroom work: as law firm Viet An reads the rules, they make no distinction between office work and work from home. Platforms based in Vietnam that hire foreign teachers are employers like any centre.

Teaching online for a company abroad is a grey area. Vietnam has no work-permit category for living in the country while working remotely for a foreign employer, and every form of work in [Decree 219, Art. 2](https://english.luatvietnam.vn/decree-no-219-2025-nd-cp-dated-august-07-2025-of-the-government-on-foreign-workers-in-vietnam-407607-doc1.html) is tied to a Vietnamese employer, partner or presence. Law firm [Viet An reads this](https://luatvietan.vn/nguoi-nuoc-ngoai-lam-viec-online-co-can-giay-phep-lao-dong-khong.html) as meaning that work for a foreign company with no commercial presence in Vietnam generally needs no Vietnamese work permit. No official statement from the Ministry of Home Affairs confirms that. Treat it as untested, and take advice from a Vietnamese lawyer before online income becomes your main income here.

Two practical points. Moving private lessons online does not change the work-permit position: Viet An notes that the law does not distinguish office work from home-based work. And online platforms make a poor substitute for local pay: Cambly's US$10.20 an hour is well below what Saigon centres pay, so treat platforms as a top-up, and check whether a platform is accepting new tutors before you plan around it.

sections.title: How side income and online income are taxed

blocks.text: Vietnam's new [Personal Income Tax Law 109/2025/QH15](https://hrspring.vn/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Van-ban-hop-nhat-112-VBHN-VPQH.pdf) applies its salary rules to the whole 2026 tax year, and [Decree 253/2026/ND-CP](https://congbaocdn.chinhphu.vn/180507251028987904/2026/7/16/469959-1784171413_v1_1784174315_signed.pdf) fills in the detail. Teaching fees count as employment income. You are **resident** if you spend 183 days or more in Vietnam in a calendar year or in the 12 months from your arrival, or if rental contracts in Vietnam add up to 183 days or more in the tax year. Residents are taxed on worldwide income at 5/10/20/30/35% on monthly taxable income up to {{vnd:10000000}} / to {{vnd:30000000}} / to {{vnd:60000000}} / to {{vnd:100000000}} / above, after a personal deduction of {{vnd:15500000}} a month. Non-residents pay a flat 20% on pay for work done in Vietnam, wherever it is paid.

blocks.text: Residents who finalise themselves file by the last day of the fourth month after the tax year; for 2026 that is 30 April 2027, a public holiday, so the deadline moves to the next working day. Since 1 July 2026, foreigners with overdue tax can be stopped from leaving Vietnam until it is paid. Withholding thresholds and residency tests are summarised by [Vialto Partners](https://vialtopartners.com/regional-alerts/vietnam-employment-tax-decree-no-253-2026-nd-cp-and-circular-no-87-2026-tt-btc-guiding-the-new-personal-income-tax-pit-law). US citizens have no treaty to rely on: Vietnam is not on the [IRS treaty list](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/international-businesses/united-states-income-tax-treaties-a-to-z), so relief comes only from US domestic rules. The [income tax guide](/teach-in-vietnam/personal-income-tax-for-teachers-in-vietnam) works through finalisation step by step.

sections.title: Finding students, getting paid and staying safe

blocks.text: Because the legal route runs through an employer, "finding students" really means finding the centre, school or company that will employ you for the extra hours.

items: **Look for part-time and cover work.** The [eno.vn jobs page](/jobs-vietnam-expats) gathers teaching postings from job boards and schools' own careers pages; you apply on the original posting, and eno.vn has not verified the employers behind them. The [Saigon school directory](/schools) lists Ho Chi Minh City employers, with reviews from teachers where they exist.

**Let schools find you for cover.** A free teacher profile, started at [teacher.eno.vn](https://teacher.eno.vn), lets you mark the periods you are free for cover work, an hourly rate and the districts you will travel to. Only schools, centres and companies can message you, and your contact details stay hidden until you choose to share them. A school that hires you for cover still needs its own work permit for you.

**Never pay to get work.** VUS says [any request for money or to download an app is a scam](https://teachenglish.vus.edu.vn/fake-job-warning), and VAS says it [never charges recruitment fees or asks candidates to open e-wallets](https://vas.edu.vn/en/news/vietnam-australia-international-school-vas-warning-about-fraudulent-recruitment-information). More signals are in [teaching job scams in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/teaching-job-scams-in-vietnam).

**Get paid like an employee.** Hourly pay under a labour contract is due after each period worked, or as an agreed lump sum at least every 15 days, with a payslip each time ([Labour Code Arts. 95 and 97](https://hethongphapluat.com/bo-luat-lao-dong-2019/dieu-97)). Get the pay date in writing, keep your own record of classes taught, and refuse any deposit or request to hand over original documents.

**One-to-one lessons with children** need the same care as classroom work: follow your employer's safeguarding policy and keep lessons where the employer has arranged them. See [safeguarding and professional conduct](/teach-in-vietnam/safeguarding-and-professional-conduct-for-teachers-in-vietnam).

**Platform money.** Cambly pays out on Tuesdays (UTC) on a 1-, 2- or 4-week cycle. Wise can send money into Vietnam but [cannot send đồng out](https://wise.com/help/articles/2571907/what-currencies-can-i-send-to-and-from), and banks send a foreigner's income abroad only up to the [documented legal income earned in Vietnam](https://www.pvcombank.com.vn/san-pham/ca-nhan/chuyen-tien-quoc-te/chuyen-thu-nhap-hop-phap-cua-ca-nhan-nguoi-nuoc-ngoai), so keep payslips and platform statements. See [banking and sending money home](/teach-in-vietnam/banking-and-sending-money-home-from-vietnam).

faqs.q: Can I give paid private lessons while my work permit is still being processed?
faqs.a: No. A foreigner may not start paid work, including probation or paid trial classes, until the work permit is issued. Working without one is fined under Decree 283/2026/ND-CP, in force since 10 September 2026, and can lead to deportation.

faqs.q: Can a school pay me as a freelancer for cover lessons?
faqs.a: Not in a way that keeps you legal. Paid work under a school's direction is a labour contract in substance whatever it is called, and covering for another school still needs that school's own work permit for you.

faqs.q: Do I pay Vietnamese tax on Cambly or Preply income?
faqs.a: If you are tax-resident, yes: residents are taxed on worldwide income, and income from a foreign payer that is not tax-registered in Vietnam must be declared and paid by you. Foreign tax can be credited only under a double tax treaty.

faqs.q: Can I tutor the pupils I teach at a public school if their parents ask?
faqs.a: No. Circular 29/2024 bars a school teacher from giving paid extra classes outside school to pupils they are assigned to teach, and lessons paid by the parents would also be work outside your permit.
